subject: Post-call recap: TCO & token economics for Acme - next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 06 Apr 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: TCO & token economics for Acme - next steps

Jordan — thanks for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned.

Pain points you shared:
- High monthly spend on embeddings + summarization flow (~$30k/month).
- Tail latency variability when multiple users hit long-context summaries.
- Hard to forecast cost spikes because of repeated prefix tokens and per-request overhead.

Goals we heard:
- Reduce monthly inference spend from ~$30k to target ~$15k while preserving quality.
- Keep 95p latency under 300ms for interactive workflows.
- Run a short pilot to validate savings before committing to reserved capacity.

High-level cost levers we discussed (what we’d model in the pilot):
- Batching: aggregate requests to reduce per-request overhead; typical uplift for this workload is 15–30% token throughput efficiency depending on distribution.
- KV/prefix caching: avoid re-sending long shared context; we’ve seen 30–50% fewer tokens served in similar enterprise knowledge-base setups.
- Model variant + quantization: moving to a 4-bit quantized medium model for cold-paths can cut per-token spend by ~30% with minor quality tradeoffs on tail cases.
- Hybrid routing: route latency-sensitive requests to a higher-SLA variant and background/async jobs to cost-optimized variants.

Immediate next steps I propose:
1) You share a representative 48–72h token log (anonymized) and a couple sample prompts. We’ll run a quick profiler to estimate batching/caching impact. (Attached: Acme_TCO_estimate_20260406.xlsx — sample template).
2) Redwood runs a 7–10 day TCO model and a cost-sensitive runbook with conservative/expected/best-case projections.
3) If the model shows meaningful savings, we’ll scope a 4-week pilot (we propose 2-week infra prep + 2-week live pilot).

Timing: I’m available next Tue/Wed morning PST for a short follow-up to confirm the token log and pilot scope.

Attachments: Acme_TCO_estimate_20260406.xlsx (sample TCO template)

Thanks — looking forward to partnering on this.

—
Marissa Cole

Subject: Re: Post-call recap: TCO & token economics for Acme - next steps

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side: 
- Current direct spend on the pipeline you saw is roughly $30k/month (embeddings + generation).
- Our procurement target for next quarter is to get operating spend below $15k/month for this feature.

Two things that will help us move:
1) Can you provide ballpark impact numbers for batching (batch=1 vs batch=8) and caching (no cache vs 40% prefix reduction)? Concrete % savings on token spend would help the finance team.
2) We need to confirm SOC2 / data handling for the pilot — security is a gating item.

If you can send a short TCO snapshot with the batching/caching scenarios, we’ll share the anonymized token logs by EOD tomorrow. Also open to the 4-week pilot you proposed.

—

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 07 Apr 2026 17:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: TCO & token economics for Acme - next steps

Jordan — great, appreciate the budget target. Below are conservative ballpark projections we’ll refine once we have your token log. I’ve included a short worked example so finance has something to run with immediately.

Worked example (high level):
- Baseline: current pipeline modeled at 1M tokens/month = $1,200/month (example pricing for the model mix you described).
- Batching: moving from per-request (batch=1) to batch=8 typically reduces per-token overhead and improves throughput; estimate = ~20–25% cost reduction on the generation portion (net ~15% reduction on total spend when blended with embeddings).
- KV/prefix caching: if we can cache shared context and avoid sending repeated 40% of prefix tokens, that’s ~40% fewer tokens billed for that portion. If prefixes account for ~30% of token volume, that’s ~12% total token reduction.
- Model variant + quant: switching cold-path traffic to a quantized medium model can reduce per-token model compute by ~30% for that slice of traffic.

Combining levers (conservative overlap assumptions):
- Conservative combined savings: 35–45% total inference cost reduction.
- Best case: 50%+ (if prefixes are large and a high percentage of requests can be batched).

Example applied to your $30k/month baseline:
- Conservative 40% reduction => ~$18k/month (saves $12k/mo).
- Further optimizations and reserved capacity pricing can push to the ~$12–15k/month target.

Security: we’re SOC 2 Type II compliant and can run the pilot under our standard pilot agreement with a Data Processing Addendum. I’ll loop in security for the SOC2 evidence and an inbound link to our compliance folder.

Next steps (concrete):
1) You send anonymized 48–72h token logs and a couple sample prompts.
2) We run an initial profiler + TCO snapshot (2–3 business days).
3) Review results in a short 30m call and finalize pilot scope.

I’ve attached a short TCO sample and a link to a shared folder: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1A2B3AcmeTCO/view

Available Wed morning or Thu afternoon PST for the follow-up call — what works for you?

—
